correctness.rationale: The dimensionless stationary process exists by a contracting pullback integral driven by an irreducible three-state chain. Generator identities imply an all-order moment recurrence, which determines the exact independent-beta-product law by compact support. Rational elimination at fixed variance yields T_s(a), whose derivative numerator has opposite signs at the endpoints of the admissible rescaled interval, hence exactly one minimum. Endpoint exclusion gives the full 0/1/2 count; the sixth-moment witness separates the two physical laws. The standalone symbolic verifier checks these algebraic identities and 48 exact rational test points; no finite sweep is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A two-parameter physical model is incompletely identifiable from its two natural low-order stationary moments. The exact fold partitions the full admissible observation plane into 0/1/2 compatible rate pairs, with a nonempty two-solution region and a sharp boundary where a finite rate is lost. A rational sixth-moment witness proves this is genuine distributional non-identifiability, relevant to calibrating active transport from stationary position measurements. The monotone radial beta-product coupling adds a structural interpretation beyond mere algebraic recovery.
